title: jon rahm uncertain about liv golf future time will tell  flm 2026 09 08
text:
Sep 08 (Field Level Media) - Jon Rahm is facing uncertainty on and off the golf course as he looks at the closing stretch of 2026 while trying to plan for the future.
Rahm will tee it up at this week's Irish Open at the Trump International Golf Links & Hotel, and plans to play in next week's BMW PGA Championship. ​What happens after that is dependent upon a slew of factors that are largely out of Rahm's control.
The Spaniard returned home after last ‌month's season-ending LIV Golf event in Indianapolis to "play dad" with his wife pregnant with the couple's fourth child. While speculation about Rahm's playing future has run rampant, he was asked only one question about LIV during his pre-tournament press conference on Tuesday, replying simply: "No updates since Indianapolis."
LIV is expected to face bankruptcy proceedings as CEO Scott O'Neil attempts to lock investors into his LIV ​2.0 concept. What that means for Rahm, and whether he would stay to have a stake in the league or is angling to get ​out of the remaining years on his contract, remains a major question mark.
Rahm said that has not been his focus during ⁠his few weeks away from the course.
"I've been a dad, basically. I got a very pregnant wife at home who is feeling this pregnancy," he said. "Unfortunately, she ​was a bit under the weather, so luckily I was home and I could step in and play dad. So it hasn't left a lot of room for ​golf.
"But at this stage of the year, having a little bit of time off and actually dealing with reality and real life, it's very nice and needed. And I was very happy to be able to be home and just take care of my kids."
Other than playing the next two events, Rahm has no firm idea of when he will compete next. Part ​of that will be determined by when his wife gives birth and if it conflicts with the Spanish Open the second week of October.
"It all depends on ​when the little one decides to arrive. I hope I can be there, but we will see," Rahm said. "It's one of those things where family always comes first, and as much ‌as I ⁠love the Spanish Open, if I have to choose, obviously it's an easy choice. But it all depends on when the little one decides to come."
The other part of the equation is the ongoing war between Iran and Israel and the United States. The conflict has already impacted multiple Formula 1 races and threatens to impact the DP World Tour's season-ending tournaments in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.
Rahm, 31, is coming off his third individual LIV Golf title in as many years since joining the ​league. He signed a deal that reportedly ​has more than $100 million remaining on ⁠it, and he acknowledged in May that it has multiple years remaining. However, he may have an option to get out of that contract with LIV Golf planning to significantly reduce prize purses should it be able to conduct a 2027 season.
As ​to whether he would be interested in pursuing a return to the PGA Tour if conditions allow, Rahm said ​in an interview with ⁠BBC Sport he's "more than willing to fulfill" his LIV 1.0 contract, but "time will tell."
Rahm struck a deal with the DP World Tour in May to retain his membership and Ryder Cup eligibility. But even that event is a year out and too far in the distance to occupy much of Rahm's mental bandwidth.
"A year is a long time. I ⁠wouldn't say ​it's that much on my mind yet," he said. "I understand why, being in Ireland, a lot of ​people are already looking forward to it, because you have to plan in advance.
"But I hope I'm representing Europe at Adare Manor, I really would love to be there, but there's just so much ​time that I haven't really given it that much thought yet. But obviously we ... a lot of us obviously want to be there and represent Europe."
--Field Level Media
